course_name_original: Allgemeine Didaktik mit Eignungs- und Orientierungspraktikum
course_name_en: General Didactics with Aptitude and Orientation Internship

learning_outcomes.text: Students understand didactics as a sub-discipline of pedagogy and can make further distinctions from neighboring and related disciplines, as well as identify subject areas and functions of didactics.
Students can differentiate between selected didactic theories and models and highlight the importance of these theoretical foundations for the planning of teaching-learning processes.
Students possess a fundamental knowledge and understanding of teaching categories and can apply them in initial planning attempts and critically evaluate them.
Students are able to transfer the steps of lesson planning and utilize them for their own teaching attempts in the aptitude and orientation internship.
Students are able to critically question this knowledge, modify the resulting questions into exploratory questions, and systematically work on them during the internship.
Students reflect on their own development process, incorporating both initial practical professional experiences and the theoretical engagement with various exploratory subjects.

syllabus_topics: Genesis, subject areas/fields of activity, basic concepts and research approaches of General Didactics
Didactic theories, e.g., educational theory didactics, learning/teaching theory didactics, constructivist didactics, curriculum didactics
Structure and planning logic of teaching
Basic forms of didactic lesson planning, implementation, and analysis
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the module examination and performance certificate. The grade's relevance to the final grade is determined by the study and examination regulations (SPO).
